about.title: Barstow Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Barstow sees steady traffic through its I-15 corridor, along with retail and lodging clusters near W Main Street, E Main Street, and Lenwood Road that serve both residents and travelers passing through. Those same properties — parking lots, entryways, motel walkways, gas station floors — are where many falls happen, often from spills, uneven pavement, poor lighting, or ignored maintenance. Under California law, a property owner isn't automatically responsible just because someone fell on their premises. You generally need to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. That's why documentation matters early: photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage can fade or disappear fast. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Barstow, we can connect you with an independent attorney who reviews what happened and explains your options at no cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney knows how to dig up maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Video and Evidence Disappear Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so an insurer may argue you weren't watching where you walked. An attorney can push back on unfair blame while still accounting for your own share.

items.question: I fell at a store near E Main Street. Do I automatically have a case?
items.answer: Not automatically — a fall alone isn't enough under California law. You'll generally need to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. An attorney can help figure out whether the facts support that.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a fall in Barstow?
items.answer: Generally two years from the date of the fall, though it can be shorter if a government entity owns the property, such as a public sidewalk or building. Missing that window can end your ability to recover anything, so it's worth checking your specific timeline soon.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall at a business?
items.answer: Photograph the hazard before anyone cleans it up, get names of any witnesses, and ask the business to preserve any surveillance video. Report the fall to management and get medical care even if you feel okay at first, since some injuries show up later.
